verses.1: And the word of Jehovah came to me, saying:
verses.2: The son of man sets your faces toward darkness; he leads you to destruction and into the forest of destruction.
verses.3: And you said to the barren forest, “Hear the words of the LORD. As Adonai Yehovah says: I will kindle fire in you. All dry trees and all thorny plants will be burned up. No one will be able to extinguish that fire. All faces of the barren land will be destroyed.”
verses.4: And all birds saw that I, the LORD, am in their midst; they will not be destroyed.
verses.5: And he said, “Ah, Adonai Yehovah! These people say to me, ‘You don’t have any power to rule.’”
verses.6: And the word of Jehovah came to me, saying:
verses.7: The son of man shall set your faces toward Jerusalem, and he shall take you to the holy places. He will lead you into the land of Israel.
verses.8: And you said to the land of Israel, “As Jehovah says: ‘I am your God. I have brought you out from Egypt. I recognize those who are righteous and those who are wicked.’”
verses.9: For I have known from you that there are both righteous and wicked people. Therefore, your destruction will come from its place, and it will be scattered among all those who are stubborn and rebellious.
verses.10: And all living things shall know that I, Jehovah, have rescued them from their destruction. They will never be destroyed again.
verses.11: And you, son of man, will sigh in sorrow, with pain and grief. You will also sigh in anguish for their eyes.
verses.12: And it shall be as if they said to you, “Why are you sad?” You will say to them, “She has come, and all hearts will be filled with sorrow. All hands will tremble, and all spirits and all blessings will be destroyed. Now she has come, and now she will become a curse for me, O Lord God.”
verses.13: And the word of Jehovah was to me, “Behold.”
verses.14: Son of Man, you are to be taken away. And you shall say, “Thus says the Lord: ‘It will be destroyed; it will be ruined.’”
verses.15: So that it may be blessed, so that it may become fresh and green again. Or so that it may become a beautiful plant, the fruit of Moaseth’s efforts. All of the trees will be blessed in this way.
verses.16: And he gave it to Marta, so that she could take it with her. It was a beautiful gift. But Marta didn’t want to give it away to anyone else.
verses.17: Cry and shout, son of man! For she was among my people. She was among all the women of Israel. They were exiled to the land of Kheresh. My people became like strangers in that land.
verses.18: For what good will it do if there is no one to serve God? My Lord, may you not allow such a thing to happen.
verses.19: And you, son of man, are brought forth. You will be raised from one place to another. You will multiply the destruction of those who are evil. It is a great destruction that will be brought upon them.
verses.20: So that I might have a heart that is pure, and so that all those who oppress them might be defeated. Therefore, I gave them a sword made of iron, a weapon that can be used for killing.
verses.21: I have united myself with the upper forces of darkness. My face is turned towards them.
verses.22: And I will also kiss with my lips against their lips. I will pour out my passion upon them. I am the LORD who speaks.
verses.23: And the word of Jehovah came to me, saying:
verses.24: And you, son of Adam, there are two paths leading to the ruin of Babylon from this land. Two people went along those paths; one went through the path that leads to the city.
verses.25: It is necessary to take care that the ruins of the children of Israel and the Jews in Jerusalem be destroyed.
verses.26: For the king of Babylon stood at the crossroads between two paths. He asked the women there, “Which path should I take?” They replied, “Look at the sign.”
verses.27: In our time, the “Kesem” was in Jerusalem, serving as a symbol of destruction. It was used to bring death upon people, to spread chaos and destruction through the gates of the city.
verses.28: And it would be like a curse in their eyes; it would bring them destruction and harm. It would also serve as a warning against falling into temptation.
verses.29: Therefore, as Adonai Yehovah has said, “Let them remember your sins, so that they may see your faults in all your deeds. Let them remember your sins, so that they may be punished for them.”
verses.30: And you are a wicked man, king of Israel. It is your time to perish in this time of disaster.
verses.31: So said Adonai Yehovah: “Remove this canopy from above me. These mountains that cover the ground are not worthy of being called mountains at all. They are nothing but low and insignificant things.”
verses.32: Ah, ah, ah! I regret it once again. It still wasn’t until then that justice was served and he was punished accordingly.
verses.33: And you, son of Adam, who have been brought forth from your mother’s womb, you said, “Thus says the Lord Jehovah to the children of men and to their ruin.” You said, “Ruin, destruction! It will be opened for slaughter, to be consumed by fire.”
verses.34: In your visions, you will see a false dream that is meant to lead you into the hands of the wicked. They will come at the time of disaster.
verses.35: Return to your dwelling place, in the place where you were created on the land of Egypt. I will deliver you from there.
verses.36: And I will pour out my wrath on you with fire. I will destroy you completely, and I will hand you over to those evil people who are full of destruction.
verses.37: Fire will become food for you. Your blood will be in the earth. Do not remember that I am Jehovah, who have spoken.
